newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - CSR sees 20 pct fall in half profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - CSR sees 20 pct fall in half profit.

text.p: CSR Ltd said on Monday that its profit for the first six months of the current financial year is likely to be 20 percent lower.
The company, which has operations in the building, sugar, and aluminium sectors, said the full year result could also be down by the same amount if the first half trend continued.
CSR said also it expected to cut its half year dividend by two cents to 12 cents per share.

"CSR's profits for the first six months are likely to be about 20 percent lower than the corresponding period last year," CSR said in a statement issued after a board meeting on Monday at which directors considered the profit outlook.
"Unless trading conditions improve, this trend will continue for the full year," the company said.

"Directors expect that if the profit for the six months ending September 1996 remains unchanged from the preliminary figures the interim diviedend will be reduced by two cents to 12 cents, 50 percent franked."
CSR said intense price competition and low volumes continued in the Autralian building products market, which was a major drag on 1995/96 (April/March) earnings.

The company said its United States operation was achieving record profits, but the aluminium group which was a strong performer last year would achieve lower earnings in 1996/97 due to falling world prices.
Sugar profits for the full year would be close to that achieved last year despite lower raw sugar prices.
CSR said profits from asset sales could assist second half profits.
CSR said its directors would formally consider a reduction in the interim dividend at their board meeting on November 11.
"A reduction in the final dividend wold also be expected unless there is a material change in profitability," the company said.
The announcement was released after the close of local trading. CSR shares ended one cent lower at A$4.53 while the overall Australian share market ended at a record closing high.
